clue.text: I'd say Satan'll wreck time of Christian celebration

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A believer worries that the devil will ruin a holy festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of 1 November honouring every saint is a fixed date in the church calendar.

clue.text: An Italian poet certainly not hurrying from bar to bar

definitions.text: certainly not hurrying from bar to bar

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian poet strolls unhurriedly from one pub to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a bar of music: the term is a tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo direction meaning at a moderate walking pace, so steady rather than rushed between measures.

clue.text: Youngsters becoming classless?

parts.note: pupils finishing school no longer belong to a class, a social-class reading being the decoy

explanation.definitionFit: School pupils who finish their education depart and so no longer belong to any class.

clue.text: Poles receiving extra money in places poles apart?

indicators.note: one piece takes in another, as a container receives contents

parts.note: anodes are electrical poles of a battery or cell
a tip is extra money given for service

explanation.surface: Polish workers earning bonuses in distant lands at opposite ends of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means electrical terminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Places diametrically opposite each other on the globe, as far apart as the two geographic extremes.

clue.text: It's black chess piece, not the king though

indicators.note: not having something means taking it away from the chess-piece word

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece
K is the chess notation for king

explanation.surface: A player notes that a dark chess piece is not the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are proverbially black, so the dark period stands for the colour.

clue.text: Marines organised for workshop

indicators.note: organising arranges things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marines are arranged into a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: A class meeting for discussion and practical study is a synonym for a workshop.

clue.text: One has a role in flying

definitions.text: One has a role in flying

indicators.note: flying here means sent scattering, so these letters are tossed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is cast in a part in an aviation show.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap on an aircraft wing controls roll, so it has a part to play in flight.

clue.text: According to report, this professional could have been beaten!

definitions.text: According to report, this professional could have been beaten!

parts.words: According to report, this professional could have been beaten!
parts.note: a press snapper working for a news report whose picture was beaten to the front page by a rival's shot

explanation.definitionFit: A professional who takes pictures, often for newspaper reports, is the person described.

clue.text: One can hear fictional murderer rave — one can turn it on

indicators.note: what is heard is a word said out loud, giving the sound of the murderer's name

parts.note: Mr Hyde, the murderous alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novel
to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: Listen to a storybook killer ranting, then the instruction to switch something on.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of HYDE gives HYD, followed by RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A street water outlet for firefighters is opened with a key so water can flow.

clue.text: Took a chance and suffered wound in leg

parts.note: gam is a slang word for a leg
bleeding is what one does from a wound

explanation.surface: A risk-taker was hurt in the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To bet or risk something on an uncertain outcome is to wager.

clue.text: Book or novel by no means odd

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book or novel described as perfectly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like part of the definition but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel about a shipping merchant and his family is a book title.

clue.text: Future at Oxford? It can make one become uneasy

parts.note: the future is a grammatical tense
a student up is in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student wonders about prospects at Oxford, making them nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow tight and anxious, stiffening with nerves, is the phrasal verb meant.

clue.text: So much French drink for a pet

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: So much French alcohol given to a beloved animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like a beloved animal, but here it is a fit of sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the old sense is a fit of pique or sulk, a childish outburst.

clue.text: Imagine people at party wasting time

indicators.note: wasting time means the time letter is lost from the word

parts.note: guests attend a party

explanation.surface: Picture partygoers idling the hours away.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose or conjecture something is a synonym for picturing it.

clue.text: Submission from legal team about to be entered

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, as one enters a room

parts.note: the defence is the lawyers acting for the accused
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A court filing from lawyers is about to be lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectful yielding to another's wishes is a form of submissiveness.

clue.text: Officer needs to get male hiding in wood, say

parts.note: fir is a type of wood

indicators.note: something hidden inside another word is placed within it

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: An officer needs to find a man concealed in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The deck officer next in rank below a ship's captain.

clue.text: Concoction of tripe and peas served as first course maybe

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dish of offal and peas is offered as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish served before the main meal, a starter, is an example of a first course.

clue.text: Show ending prematurely with nothing wrong? That's a mystery

indicators.note: stopping too soon means the last letter of the show word is dropped

parts.note: a parade is a show or display
O looks like zero, so stands for nothing
X is the mark put against something wrong

explanation.surface: A performance closing early for no reason is puzzling.
explanation.definitionFit: A seemingly self-contradictory statement or situation is a puzzle or enigma.

clue.text: Flog sailor heartlessly with cat

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the sailor word goes

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A sailor is cruelly whipped with a cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat suggests a whip, but it is the animal. TAR loses its middle A to give TR.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat thoroughly or defeat heavily is a slang sense of flogging.

clue.text: Dad's Army's food (not as supplied by Jones though!)

parts.note: pa is dad, with the possessive giving PA'S
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: The food in a sitcom, not what its butcher character supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; Jones is its butcher, who supplies meat, hence the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian dough products such as spaghetti are a staple foodstuff.

clue.text: Country person producing vegetables — hill worker?

parts.note: peas are vegetables
a worker ant lives in an anthill

explanation.surface: A rural dweller grows vegetables and works the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hill worker' suggests a hill farmer, but it is an insect from an anthill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural farm labourer of low social standing is a person of the countryside.

clue.text: Smashing FT is read no end — likely to carry on fine!

indicators.note: smashing breaks things to pieces, so these letters are rearranged
no end means the last letter is dropped from the word read

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A great FT forecast is read as promising good weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts READ to REA, which joins FTIS for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer marking for settled weather, so the fine spell is expected to continue.

clue.text: A funny brother performing — one Ahab's worked with?

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A comic sibling on stage, perhaps aboard a whaler.
explanation.walkthrough: Ahab is the whaling captain of Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Ahab hunted the whale with the barbed spear thrown by whalers.

clue.text: Second-generation American in Washington is eighty

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A second-generation American in the capital turns eighty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese-American born in the US to immigrant parents is a second-generation citizen.

clue.text: Like certain food that's sampled — contains egg

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: to sample food is to taste it
O resembles an egg in shape

explanation.surface: A dish that has been tried has an egg in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Browned by heat, as bread or nuts are, describes certain foods.

clue.text: Travelling south from Yorkshire?

parts.note: riding is travelling on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: Heading south out of a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large English county, was historically divided into three administrative parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic North, East and West divisions of the county together make up the whole region.

clue.text: Indians producing a type of modern music at front of a house

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the next in the answer

parts.note: rap is a modern music genre

explanation.surface: Natives play contemporary music outside a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the Great Plains, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: Scientist no longer on edge has secured reputation finally

parts.note: ex describes something former, no longer current

indicators.note: the edge word holds the letter firmly within it

parts.note: a perimeter is an edge or boundary

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of reputation

explanation.surface: A former scientist on edge holds onto his good name at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who carries out tests to try ideas is a type of scientist.
